exposure: Uterine closure technique during cesarean delivery (two-layer endometrium-free closure vs. two- or one-layer routine closures)
outcome: Prevalence and severity of postcesarean residual niche
Risk of placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) disorders
cohort: 70 women who had one prior cesarean delivery and underwent saline infusion sonohysterography.
finding: Uterine closure techniques are associated with the development and size of postcesarean residual niches, and an endometrium-free closure technique during primary cesarean delivery is associated with a reduced risk of future niche formation and PAS complications.
mod_finding: The study found that using an endometrium-free closure technique during cesarean delivery was associated with smaller niche dimensions and a lower incidence of clinically significant niches.
followup_time: N/A (observations were taken at some unspecified time after a prior cesarean delivery)
cross-section timing: At the time of saline infusion sonohysterography after one prior cesarean delivery (specific postpartum interval not specified)
